title: Paradoxon From Elsbethen
author: Peter Siegfried Krug
synopsis: The Glasenbach Years and Social Decline (1982–1987) The Paradox of Elsbethen: An Analysis of Trauma Reactivation and Social Exclusion Documentation of the life of Peter Siegfried Krug (born 1966) This report analyzes the critical period between the ages of 16 and 21. It describes how a highly gifted young man, shaped by severe institutional violence (orphanages/group homes), fell into total social exclusion despite intellectual resources and short-term professional success. I. Lohäuslweg 9: The Philosophical Refuge (ca. 1982–1983) After the loss of housing at Sinnhubstraße, the room at Lohäuslweg marked a phase of rural isolation . This period was characterized by an extreme dualism between physical neglect and high intellectual culture. Living Conditions & Health: A diet consisting of instant coffee, yogurt chocolate, and Coca-Cola led to massive physical emaciation and chronic somatic complaints. Social interaction was limited to conflicts in the shared kitchen with an alcoholic roommate. Mental Resilience: Isolation was compensated for through the intensive study of Nietzsche ( Twilight of the Idols ), Schopenhauer, and Lao Tzu. Engaging with chess compositions (studies by Mattison and Kaminer) and correspondence with Werner Speckmann served as order-providing elements in an unstable reality. Human Anchors: Landlady Gerhild Hirnsperger and her family offered the only emotional bridge to normalcy. The nature of the Glasenbachklamm (gorge) functioned as a psychological sanctuary. II. The Paradox of Elsbethen: Trauma Reactivation in the Workplace The attempt to establish a career as a kindergarten teacher in Elsbethen illustrates the failure of integration when conducted without trauma-pedagogical support. Success as a Trigger: Professional aptitude and popularity (documented by contemporary radio interviews) masked internal instability. The carefree nature of the children acted as a massive emotional trigger for his own childhood traumas (e.g., Guggenthal). The Psychological Collapse: The inability to separate professional life from private trauma led to obsessive thought patterns and eventually incapacity to act . Standing paralyzed for 15 minutes in front of the kindergarten gate symbolizes the psyche's final resistance against an environment perceived as an emotional minefield. III. Criminalization and Pre-trial Detention: Schanzelgasse 1 The loss of professional structure resulted in a phase of anomie and petty crime. Systemic Degradation: Detention at the Salzburg Regional Court (Schanzelgasse 1) was characterized by repressive interrogation methods (sleep/light deprivation) and depressive episodes culminating in a suicide attempt. Literary Escape: Despite cognitive limitations due to prison stress, literature (Shakespeare, Zweig) remained the final means of self-assertion. Release at Christmas was only made possible through third-party bail. IV. "Alter Fuchs" and Total Homelessness (1984–1987) The final phase describes the definitive break with bourgeois society. Loss of Cultural Capital: Upon eviction from the "Alter Fuchs" guesthouse, the private library was lost. This marked the transition from "impoverished intellectual" to "invisible homeless person." Physical Survival: The years 1984–1987 were marked by nights spent in horse carriages (Obergnigl) during extreme cold. Shame functioned as a social barrier that prevented any search for help. Flight into the mountains was an attempt at physical numbing of psychological pain. Analysis: Why Integration Failed Lack of Titration: Confrontation with the theme of "childhood" in the workplace occurred too abruptly and without therapeutic dosage. Structural Failure: The social system relied on "healing through work" without considering the specific burden of re-traumatization in care-giving professions. Dehumanization by Institutions: The rapid shift from media recognition to criminalizing detention illustrates the fragility of social identity for former victims of institutional violence. Glossary & Sources Twilight of the Idols ( Götzendämmerung ): A late work by Friedrich Nietzsche (1889); a radical revaluation of all values, used by Krug as an intellectual tool to break free from religious dogmas. Re-traumatization: The uncontrolled re-experiencing of past traumatic events triggered by current stimuli. Schanzelgasse 1: Historical location of the Salzburg Regional Court prison. Sources: Biographical reconstruction based on personal records, witness accounts (Gerhild Hirnsperger), and documents regarding the period of detention (1980s). About the Author / Mission: Peter Siegfried Krug documents his biography as a survivor of institutional violence in Austrian group homes. The goal of this work is the seamless processing of the long-term consequences of abuse and the visualization of the mechanisms of social decline to raise awareness for the necessity of trauma-pedagogical support.

Flight into the mountains was an attempt at physical numbing of psychological pain. Analysis: Why Integration Failed Lack of Titration: Confrontation with the theme of "childhood" in the workplace occurred too abruptly and without therapeutic dosage. Structural Failure: The social system relied on "healing through work" without considering the specific burden of re-traumatization in care-giving professions. Dehumanization by Institutions: The rapid shift from media recognition to criminalizing detention illustrates the fragility of social identity for former victims of institutional violence. Glossary & Sources Twilight of the Idols ( Götzendämmerung ): A late work by Friedrich Nietzsche (1889); a radical revaluation of all values, used by Krug as an intellectual tool to break free from religious dogmas. Re-traumatization: The uncontrolled re-experiencing of past traumatic events triggered by current stimuli. Schanzelgasse 1: Historical location of the Salzburg Regional Court prison. Sources: Biographical reconstruction based on personal records, witness accounts (Gerhild Hirnsperger), and documents regarding the period of detention (1980s). About the Author / Mission: Peter Siegfried Krug documents his biography as a survivor of institutional violence in Austrian group homes. The goal of this work is the seamless processing of the long-term consequences of abuse and the visualization of the mechanisms of social decline to raise awareness for the necessity of trauma-pedagogical support.

title: PARALYZED BY SUDDEN UNCERTAINTY
author: Emil West
synopsis: PARALYZED BY SUDDEN UNCERTAINTY GIOVANNI METRO STOP GALLERY WWWG PRODUCTIONS LTD. 2025 There will inevitably come a poignant moment when you must confront the unsettling truth that most of the people you once knew have long since passed away, leading you to ponder your own mortality and the possibility that you may not be far behind them. At this juncture, you find yourself at a crossroads, paralyzed by the sudden uncertainty of which direction to take in life. This realization can be both daunting and transformative, urging you to reflect on your choices and the legacy you wish to leave behind. This circumstance, I must emphasize, is not the result of some ominous sense of fate, nor is it an acknowledgment of any personal shortcomings in willpower. It is not born from regret over my numerous missteps along what that classic rock singer referred to as "The Highway to Hell." You simply cannot grasp the depth of this experience, as you have yet to witness the haunting reality of the Valley of the Living Dead. At the crossroads, shrouded in the shadows of a forest filled with charred, hanging trees that silently judge your choices, a whisper emerges—an echo of the grievances of those you have wronged and the hollow pursuits of your self-interest. From the darkness, a semi-divine figure materializes, reminiscent of vintage 1950s science fiction illustrations. With a smile that suggests familiarity, it greets you as an old friend, yet there's a hint of annoyance in its demeanor, as if to say you've taken far too long to arrive. What other option do you have but to initiate a conversation? Would it not be impolite to genuinely ask about his well-being and that of the other demi-gods? The thought of panicking might cross your mind, but running away would lead you nowhere. Should you consider retreating into the shadows of your past, yearning for a time when you held power? This Valley of the Living Dead is not a place to escape; instead, it beckons you to engage and confront the present. Would you confront this mythical beast with the same fearless spirit you displayed on the Alamo's walls during Maximilian's final assault? Hold on! That never happened! It seems this narrative is spiraling into one of those clichéd "Choose Your Own Adventure" stories, where you're invited to play the role of a deity, transforming your mundane existence into an epic saga. Imagine a tale so grand that even Ulysses and his crew would watch in envy as you triumphantly parade through Rome, laden with treasure chests filled with the spoils of your conquests against the Old Sea Father. It appears the Red Curry Pancake Paste has ignited a surge of false bravado within me, making me feel invincible enough to traverse the Valley of the Living Dead unscathed. This Red Curry Pancake Paste Mixture is truly something remarkable, wouldn't you agree? My numerous and often harsh critics are quick to swarm like bees, furiously typing away on social media from the comfort of their parents' basements. They eagerly assert that my words are merely the result of substance use, claiming that "normal" individuals would have simply asked the bartender for their tab and headed home to their waiting families. Having recently revisited this introduction multiple times, I feel a sense of pride in how these brief paragraphs effectively convey the triviality of my role at the prestigious Columbia School of Journalism (The Home Study Course). It's amusing to recall how often I was urged not to abandon my day job. So, who's truly being petty now, Herr Professor? It's clear now that I should let go of the last part of our discussion, as you were right all along—she is indeed no longer with us. Perhaps I should venture into the depths of this metaphorical valley of the Living Dead to search for her. Yet, what would I even say? It would only serve to belittle her, reminding her that I am still alive, breathing in the remnants of life while she is not. She would undoubtedly rush to correct my choice of action verbs and mock my inability to grasp basic sentence structures. To be honest, I could easily go through life without a deceased professor criticizing my shortcomings in writing proper English. Ultimately, what would be the point of such an exercise, other than to squander more time in a metaphorical graveyard tangled with the toxic vines of regret? It seems futile to revisit the "What if?" scenarios of an old man's misguided need to rehash past decisions, believing that it could somehow alter the role I was destined to play from the moment of my birth. Emil, it's time to focus as you craft this narrative; don't shy away from the challenge or distort history to fit your current perceptions of truth. Sir Winston Churchill once addressed a young reporter from the London Times who inquired about how future generations would interpret World War Two. After a thoughtful pause, Churchill conveyed a powerful insight: the narrative of history is shaped by those who emerge victorious. This serves as a reminder that the lens through which we view the past can be influenced by the outcomes of conflict, urging you to approach your writing with integrity and depth. The demi-god, noticing my apparent distraction, grew impatient and abruptly interrupted my moment of introspection. He pointed out, referencing his computer, that I had several outstanding restraining orders from the Southern District Court. Reading from one, he sternly reminded me that I am prohibited from coming within 500 meters of the Memorial Satan Transit Camp, a place touted as the Multiverse's equivalent of Las Vegas—a playground for those seeking indulgence from the eight spheres. He further elaborated that the same order bars me from loitering at the entrance of a gated community falsely marketed as paradise, despite the once-gilded streets being long destroyed to fund St. Michael's relentless battles against evil and the torment of fallen angels confined to what locals call Earth. As a founding member of the once-outlawed Jesuits of Truth, I find myself navigating the desolate landscape of reality, much like a vampire in search of meaning. Despite the criticism from those who dismiss my status, I have the validation of a biologist to back me up. Today, as I made my way back to my modest apartment, I felt the weight of a semi-divine figure urging me to leave, his voice echoing a warning that I was no longer welcome. Upon returning, I was confronted by my intimidating landlady and her unusually large nephews, freshly released from a FEMA Re-Training facility, who were demanding payment for my overdue rent—an amount that she claimed represented several months of neglect. In that moment, I came to understand that the true torment lies in the present. Spare your prayers for my soul, which I relinquished long ago, and for my life, which I seem to have leased out to reckless tenants intent on ruining it. In summary, the elder monk cautioned me against the alluring light and warmth of the tunnel, warning that it serves as a deceptive trap leading to the cycle of reincarnation. He advised me to turn left and peer into the dark void, where I would uncover the boundaries of the Demi-god's matrix. He also urged me not to trust the familiar faces of deceased loved ones, as they are merely projections from my own memories. My subsequent experiences confirmed his wisdom; many of those who appeared to guide me toward the light were individuals I had little affection for, or those I owed money to, which they would not have so easily forget. Ultimately, my deliverance came through the restraining orders issued by the Heavenly Hosts and the representatives of Hell Incorporated Ltd., following my groundbreaking revelations that exposed in my book "Postcards from Hell" the longstanding deception of Hell and Satan as a millennia-old fraud.

title: Pariser Katzen - Bohème, Kunst und Legenden
author: Cat Man (Booklet's)
synopsis: Pariser Katzen – Bohème, Kunst und Legenden ist eine kulturhistorische Annäherung an die Rolle der Katze im Paris des 19. und frühen 20. Jahrhunderts. Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Viertel von Montmartre, das Cabaret Le Chat Noir, Künstlerateliers, Salons und Straßenszenen der Belle Époque, in denen Katzen allgegenwärtige Begleiter des städtischen Lebens waren. Das Booklet verbindet historische Texte mit realistisch-illustrierten Bildern und beleuchtet, wie Katzen zu Symbolen der Bohème, zu Motiven der Kunst und zu stillen Beobachtern gesellschaftlicher Veränderungen wurden. Dabei reicht der Blick von verwilderten Randgebieten über bürgerliche Innenräume bis hin zu den Dächern und Gassen der Stadt. Dieses Werk ist kein Reiseführer, sondern eine visuelle und erzählerische Kulturgeschichte der Pariser Katze – zwischen Alltag, Mythos und Kunst.

title: Pequenos Mundos
author: Augusto La Fere
synopsis: Pequenos Mundos reúne microcontos que tratam o cotidiano como matéria viva: instantes mínimos, gestos discretos, silêncios que vibram e aquilo que sobra depois do dia. Em textos breves e precisos, a narrativa recorta cenas comuns — casa, rua, trabalho, deslocamentos, encontros e perdas — no ponto exato em que o banal se abre e deixa ver um núcleo de estranheza, beleza ou inquietação. A obra se constrói como um mosaico de “mundos” autônomos, mas comunicantes. Cada microconto funciona como lâmina: um corte rápido que expõe afetos contidos, hábitos, ritos diários e fragmentos de memória. O humor é seco quando precisa; a ternura, contida; a emoção, mais sugerida do que declarada. Não há dependência de enredo longo: o livro aposta na intensidade do breve, na atmosfera e na reverberação. Leitura ágil na superfície, mas feita para reentrada: os textos retornam ao leitor como pequenos ecos — e, no conjunto, compõem um mapa íntimo do que permanece quando tudo parece passar.

title: Personal Cognitive Atlas – Ein strukturelles Framework zur multidimensionalen Analyse der menschlichen Persönlichkeit
author: Res Christian Manz
synopsis: Der Personal Cognitive Atlas ist ein konzeptionelles Framework zur systematischen Kartierung und Analyse der menschlichen Persönlichkeit über mehrere Dimensionen hinweg. Das Modell integriert Erkenntnisse aus Psychologie, Neurowissenschaften, Verhaltenswissenschaft, Philosophie und Systemtheorie, um eine strukturierte Methode zur Beschreibung der Persönlichkeit in ihrer gesamten Komplexität zu ermöglichen. Statt Persönlichkeit auf einzelne Eigenschaften oder isolierte Theorien zu reduzieren, organisiert der Atlas Persönlichkeit als ein Netzwerk miteinander verbundener Domänen. Dazu gehören unter anderem: kognitive Strukturen emotionale Dynamiken biologische und physiologische Systeme Entwicklungsprozesse zwischenmenschliche Beziehungen Werte- und Motivationssysteme kulturelle Einflüsse philosophische und existenzielle Orientierung Der Persönlichkeits-Atlas basiert auf einer mehrschichtigen Struktur. Diese umfasst grundlegende Domänen, spezifische Kategorien, detaillierte Aspekte sowie analytische Fragen, mit denen Persönlichkeitsstrukturen systematisch untersucht werden können. Ziel dieses Frameworks ist es, eine Grundlage für zukünftige Forschung, Selbstanalyse und interdisziplinäre Persönlichkeitsmodelle zu schaffen. Der Atlas versteht Persönlichkeit als komplexes adaptives System , dessen Struktur aus der Wechselwirkung biologischer, psychologischer, sozialer und kultureller Prozesse entsteht. Der Personal Cognitive Atlas stellt einen strukturellen Prototyp für zukünftige multidimensionale Persönlichkeitsmodelle dar und kann als Grundlage für Forschung, Selbstanalyse und interdisziplinäre Persönlichkeitsstudien dienen.

title: Pět neděl v baloně
author: Jules Verne
synopsis: Příběh o statečnosti, touze objevovat, o vynalézavosti a přátelství vypráví dobrodružství trojice hrdinů, kteří podniknou během pěti týdnů výzkumnou cestu napříč africkým kontinentem v koši polořiditelného balonu. Nad pevninou tehdy ještě neprobádané Afriky jsou doktor Fergusson a jeho přátelé svědky neuvěřitelných zážitků s domorodým obyvatelstvem, bojují se zvířaty i přírodními živly a překonávají nejrozmanitější potíže. Vedle dramatického putování je v knize vykreslen charakter krajiny, jsou zde popsány místní zvířata a rostliny a čtenář se dozví o různých objevných cestách, které byly do 60. let 19. stol. v Africe uskutečněny.

synopsis: This aviation-themed story revolves around high-flying adventures and the challenges faced by pilots in a competitive environment. The main topic of the book is the thrill of flight, punctuated by a romantic subplot and the tensions of an upcoming air race. The story follows Jane Alton, a passionate aviator, as she seeks to prove her flying skills and support her romantic interest, Ned Knight, who is set to compete in a crucial air derby. When Ned falls incapacitated due to foul play from a rival competitor, Jane disguises herself in her mechanic Benny's flying gear and takes control of their plane, the Alton, during the race. Her incredible skills and determination allow her to navigate through intense competition and hostility, ultimately leading to her victory. The book intertwines elements of adventure, romance, and suspense as it showcases Jane's journey to becoming a heroine in aviation and gaining acceptance in a male-dominated field.

title: Pourquoi Dieu nous enjoint-Il de l'adorer ? Réponse à l'objection athée qui évacue toute sagesse derrière le Premier Commandement divin à la base du monothéisme
author: Sami 'Ameri
synopsis: Le rôle approprié du savoir est de nous placer face à notre incrédulité et à notre petitesse. Chaque questionnement sensé sur les mystères de la vie offre des perspectives de raisonnement incommensurables et parfois hors de portée. Chaque prouesse scientifique complexifie notre vision des mécanismes du monde déjà extrêmement sophistiqués. Chaque jour, le laboratoire grandeur nature qui nous fait écarquiller les yeux gagne du terrain vers la connaissance du Grand Ordonnanceur qui signe chacune de Ses œuvres. Les avancées scientifiques sont des coups de massue sur l'ego afin d'assainir son orgueil et le ramener à la réalité inéluctable qu'il n'est que le spectateur du héros véritable qui se cache derrière les joyaux de la création. Le Dr Sami ‘Ameri, né en 1975, est d’origine tunisienne. Il obtient un doctorat en religions comparées, et se consacre à des ouvrages, des conférences et des recherches dans son domaine d’expertise (il a aussi développé des compétences dans la critique des idéologies modernes). Il est l’un des fondateurs de l’initiative de recherches académiques en matière de religions comparées dont il est le superviseur scientifique. Son domaine d’investigation est la théologie comparative, les idéologies modernes et l’orientalisme (l’islamologie) pour lesquels il donne des écrits et des interventions audiovisuelles. Il est un ancien membre du corps enseignant du Graduate Theological Foundation (GTF). Il est titulaire d’un doctorat à la Graduate Theological Foundation (GTF) et prépare actuellement deux autres thèses doctorantes qu’il devrait soutenir prochainement ; l’une à l’UPAFA (Université Privée Africaine Franco-Arabe) et l’autre à l’Institut Européen des Sciences Humaines de Paris. La maitrise de plusieurs langues (arabe, anglais, français, hébreu thoraïque, syriaque, et grec classique) lui élargit de façon vertigineuse son champ d’investigation.

title: Pranayama; From The Cave To Yoga
author: Da Silva
synopsis: Here is the presentation text for Internet Archive , specifically tailored for an American English-speaking audience. It uses academic and descriptive language suitable for long-term archiving and research. Title: Pranayama; From the Cave to Yoga — At the Origins of Spiritual Consciousness Description: This essay explores the prehistoric roots of spirituality and prāṇāyāma (the science of breath) through the dual lenses of neuro-archaeology and the phenomenology of the breath . The text transports the reader 16,000 years into the past, into the heart of the decorated caves of the Upper Paleolithic . It posits that the technical gesture of the shaman—spraying pigments from the mouth in a state of hypercapnia and trance—represents the foundational act of human religiosity. Key themes include: Biological Evolution: The impact of the domestication of fire on the development of the cranial brain in relation to the enteric brain. Phenomenology of the Breath: The lived experience of the breathing body as a tool for creation (parietal art) and an entry point to the sacred. The Missing Link: The connection between Stone Age shamanic practices and the yogic traditions of the Indus Valley. Comparative Religion: Parallels between the "breath of life" in Genesis and the ritual use of psychoactive substances ( gañjā , peyote, ayahuasca, and fly agaric). This work offers a unique perspective at the intersection of anthropology, evolutionary biology, and Eastern philosophy, redefining yoga not as a late invention, but as the formalization of a millenary respiratory experience.

title: Precision Public Health Applications of Whole-Exome Sequencing for Sickle Cell Disease: Evidence, Equity, and Implementation Challenges from Bench to Population (www.kiu.ac.ug)
author: Kagambira Zimbuga M.
synopsis: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a monogenic hematologic disorder that causes significant morbidity and mortality worldwide, disproportionately affecting populations of African, Indian, Middle Eastern, and Mediterranean ancestry. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) offers a precision public health approach by identifying both primary HBB mutations and modifier genes that influence disease severity, clinical complications, and therapeutic response. This paper synthesizes the evidence supporting WES for SCD, explores equity considerations in genomics implementation, and examines challenges in translating bench discoveries to population-level interventions. Key barriers include infrastructural limitations, workforce capacity, regulatory compliance, and the underrepresentation of marginalized populations in genomic studies. Case studies from Quebec, Australia, and Nordic countries highlight strategies for successful implementation, including integration with public health priorities, cross-sector collaboration, and data governance. Future research should focus on understanding genetic modifiers across diverse populations, evaluating intervention efficacy, and ensuring equitable access to genomics informed care. By aligning precision medicine with public health objectives, WES has the potential to reduce disease burden, improve health equity, and inform scalable interventions for SCD globally.

title: Pro Git [electronic resource]
author: Chacon, Scott, author, Straub, Ben, author, SpringerLink (Online service)
synopsis: Pro Git (Second Edition) is your fully-updated guide to Git and its usage in the modern world. Git has come a long way since it was first developed by Linus Torvalds for Linux kernel development. It has taken the open source world by storm since its inception in 2005, and this book teaches you how to use it like a pro. Effective and well-implemented version control is a necessity for successful web projects, whether large or small. With this book you’ll learn how to master the world of distributed version workflow, use the distributed features of Git to the full, and extend Git to meet your every need. Written by Git pros Scott Chacon and Ben Straub, Pro Git (Second Edition) builds on the hugely successful first edition, and is now fully updated for Git version 2.0, as well as including an indispensable chapter on GitHub. It’s the best book for all your Git needs. What you’ll learn Effectively use Git, either as a programmer or a project leader Become a fluent Git user Master branching, using Git on the server, and on other systems Integrate Git in your development workflow Migrate programming projects from other SCMs to Git Extend Git for your personal project needs Effectively use GitHub This book is for all open source developers: you are bound to encounter Git somewhere in the course of your working life. Proprietary software developers will appreciate Git’s enormous scalability, since it is used for the Linux project, which comprises thousands of developers and testers. Print versions available via links on the git-scm website . See also the first edition , which has been translated into 한국어 , Deutsch , 日本語 , Русский , français , 简体中文 and other languages.

title: Projected El Niño (2026)
author: Dr. James Hansen
synopsis: Crossing Earth's Rubicon ▪ White paper by the climate research scientist Dr. James Hansen - published on March 20th, 2026. Abstract: ▪ Models are converging on prediction of an El Niño beginning this year, peaking in early 2027. ▪ El Niño strength and frequency are important, especially the issue of whether these are modified by global warming . ▪ However, the more important knowledge that needs to be extracted from near-term global warming concerns the interpretation of ongoing, extraordinary, acceleration of ocean surface warming .

title: Projected Global Temperatures (2025)
author: Dr. James Hansen
synopsis: 89 Seconds to Midnight ▪ White paper by the climate research scientist Dr. James Hansen - published on April 15th, 2025. Abstract: ▪ Global temperature for 2025 should decline little, if at all, from the record 2024 level. ▪ Absence of a large temperature decline after the huge El Nino-spurred temperature increase in 2023-24 will provide further confirmation that IPCC’s best estimates for climate sensitivity and aerosol climate forcing were both underestimates . ▪ Specifically, 2025 global temperature should remain near or above +1.5°C (+2.7°F) relative to 1880-1920, and, if the tropics remain ENSO-neutral, there is good chance that 2025 may even exceed the 2024 record high global temperature.

title: Propaganda
author: Edward L. Bernays
synopsis: “Bernays' honest and practical manual provides much insight into some of the most powerful and influential institutions of contemporary industrial state capitalist democracies.”—Noam Chomsky “The conscious and intelligent manipulation of the organized habits and opinions of the masses is an important element in democratic society. Those who manipulate this unseen mechanism of society constitute an invisible government which is the true ruling power of our country.”—Edward Bernays, Propaganda A seminal and controversial figure in the history of political thought and public relations, Edward Bernays (1891–1995), pioneered the scientific technique of shaping and manipulating public opinion, which he famously dubbed “engineering of consent.” During World War I, he was an integral part of the U.S. Committee on Public Information (CPI), a powerful propaganda apparatus that was mobilized to package, advertise and sell the war to the American people as one that would “Make the World Safe for Democracy.” The CPI would become the blueprint in which marketing strategies for future wars would be based upon Bernays applied the techniques he had learned in the CPI and, incorporating some of the ideas of Walter Lipmann, became an outspoken proponent of propaganda as a tool for democratic and corporate manipulation of the population. His 1928 bombshell Propaganda lays out his eerily prescient vision for using propaganda to regiment the collective mind in a variety of areas, including government, politics, art, science and education. To read this book today is to frightfully comprehend what our contemporary institutions of government and business have become in regards to organized manipulation of the masses. This is the first reprint of Propaganda in over 30 years and features an introduction by Mark Crispin Miller, author of The Bush Dyslexicon: Observations on a National Disorder.

title: Provenienz. Forschung International
author: Robert Ketterer (ed.), Nadine Bauer, Hilde Bøe, Sabine Disterheft, Franziska Eschenbach, Carolin Faude-Nagel, Katharina Hüls-Valenti, Stephan Klingen, Sonja Niederacher, Toshiharu Omuka, Agnes Thum und Katharina Thurmair
synopsis: Dieser Sammelband führt in die internationale Welt der Provenienzforschung ein und macht sichtbar, wie weit verzweigt die Wege von Kunstwerken, Händler*innen und Sammler*innen schon lange vor der globalisierten Gegenwart waren – und wie weit auch Forschende heute „reisen“ müssen, um die Geschichten hinter den Objekten zu entschlüsseln. Die Texte eröffnen Ein­blicke in globale Kunst­handels­netz­werke, in Samm­lungs­geschichten des deutschen Expressionismus, in Verflechtungen zwischen Europa, Amerika und Japan sowie in die Folgen von NS-Verfolgung und Exil. Gleichzeitig zeigen sie, wie wesentlich der Blick über nationale Grenzen hinaus für ein umfassendes Verständnis historischer Provenienzen ist. Mit „Provenienz. Forschung international“ legt das Auktionshaus Ketterer Kunst den zweiten Band seiner wissenschaftlichen Reihe „Provenienzforschung & Kunsthandel“ vor und gewährt vertiefte Einblicke in die eigene Forschungsarbeit sowie in internationale Kooperationen. Nach dem ersten Band, der 2023 anlässlich des 25-jährigen Jubiläums der Washingtoner Prinzipien erschien und 2024 in englischer Über­setzung publiziert wurde, richtet die neue Veröffent­lichung den Fokus konsequent auf die globale Dimension der Provenienz­forschung und rückt die Zusammen­arbeit der Forschenden in Kunst­handel, Museen und Forschungs­einrichtungen über Landes­grenzen hinweg in den Mittelpunkt. In fünf thematischen Kapiteln – Japan, Norwegen, Deutschland, Italien und „Kunsthandel international“ – blicken renommierte Gastautor*innen auf internationale Künstler- und Kunsthändlerarchive, auf erhaltene Unterlagen eines deutschen Kunstsammlers, auf die Situation der deutschen Kunst in Japan um den ersten Weltkrieg sowie auf Italiens Kunsthandel in der Zeit des Nationalsozialismus. Ergänzend präsentieren die Mitarbeiter*innen der hauseigenen Abteilung Provenienzforschung von Ketterer Kunst anhand von Fallbeispielen die Wichtigkeit des kollegialen Aus­tauschs mit euro­päischen sowie außer­euro­päischen Partnern und geben darüber hinaus Einblicke in die Forschungs­vielfalt der Abteilung. „Provenienz. Forschung international“ richtet sich gleichermaßen an Wissen­schaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler wie an ein breiteres, kunst­interessiertes Publikum. Der Band bietet fundierte Einblicke in aktuelle, teils spektakuläre Provenienz­fälle, zeichnet internationale Recherche­wege nach und macht nach­voll­ziehbar, mit welcher akribischen, bisweilen detektivischen Methodik Kunstwerke und Archiv­bestände untersucht werden. Zugleich wird die grenz­über­schreitende Dimension der Provenienz­forschung anschaulich erfahrbar. Über die spannende Lektüre hinaus besitzt die Publikation auch einen praktischen Nutzen: Zahlreiche konkret benannte nationale und internationale Quellen sowie Archiv­bestände ermöglichen Forschenden, diese Materialien gezielt für die eigene Arbeit heranzuziehen.

Nach dem ersten Band, der 2023 anlässlich des 25-jährigen Jubiläums der Washingtoner Prinzipien erschien und 2024 in englischer Über­setzung publiziert wurde, richtet die neue Veröffent­lichung den Fokus konsequent auf die globale Dimension der Provenienz­forschung und rückt die Zusammen­arbeit der Forschenden in Kunst­handel, Museen und Forschungs­einrichtungen über Landes­grenzen hinweg in den Mittelpunkt. In fünf thematischen Kapiteln – Japan, Norwegen, Deutschland, Italien und „Kunsthandel international“ – blicken renommierte Gastautor*innen auf internationale Künstler- und Kunsthändlerarchive, auf erhaltene Unterlagen eines deutschen Kunstsammlers, auf die Situation der deutschen Kunst in Japan um den ersten Weltkrieg sowie auf Italiens Kunsthandel in der Zeit des Nationalsozialismus. Ergänzend präsentieren die Mitarbeiter*innen der hauseigenen Abteilung Provenienzforschung von Ketterer Kunst anhand von Fallbeispielen die Wichtigkeit des kollegialen Aus­tauschs mit euro­päischen sowie außer­euro­päischen Partnern und geben darüber hinaus Einblicke in die Forschungs­vielfalt der Abteilung. „Provenienz. Forschung international“ richtet sich gleichermaßen an Wissen­schaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler wie an ein breiteres, kunst­interessiertes Publikum. Der Band bietet fundierte Einblicke in aktuelle, teils spektakuläre Provenienz­fälle, zeichnet internationale Recherche­wege nach und macht nach­voll­ziehbar, mit welcher akribischen, bisweilen detektivischen Methodik Kunstwerke und Archiv­bestände untersucht werden. Zugleich wird die grenz­über­schreitende Dimension der Provenienz­forschung anschaulich erfahrbar. Über die spannende Lektüre hinaus besitzt die Publikation auch einen praktischen Nutzen: Zahlreiche konkret benannte nationale und internationale Quellen sowie Archiv­bestände ermöglichen Forschenden, diese Materialien gezielt für die eigene Arbeit heranzuziehen.

title: Quando A Metáfora Falha Uma Crítica Biológica Ao Cisne De Popper
author: Marcio Alexandre Afonso Polizelli
synopsis: Resumo Este artigo propõe uma reflexão crítica sobre a famosa metáfora do “cisne negro” de Karl Popper, amplamente utilizada para ilustrar o princípio da falsificabilidade científica. A partir de uma análise biológica e taxonômica, o texto argumenta que a metáfora se apoia em uma indução disfarçada e em uma definição imprecisa do termo “cisne”. O cisne-negro (Cygnus atratus) e o cisne-branco (Cygnus olor) pertencem a espécies distintas, o que compromete a validade da refutação proposta por Popper. A crítica se estende a outros exemplos zoológicos — como garças, papagaios, maritacas, araras, gatos e cães — para mostrar como nomes populares podem agrupar espécies diferentes sob uma mesma designação, gerando confusões conceituais. O artigo conclui que a força de uma refutação científica depende da clareza dos termos utilizados, e que metáforas mal formuladas podem fragilizar o método científico ao confundir ajustes de linguagem com descobertas empíricas. Palavras chaves: Filosofia da ciência, Falsificabilidade, Indução, Metáforas científicas, Taxonomia, Cisne negro, Karl Popper, Linguagem científica, Espécies biológicas, Precisão conceitual. Abstract (em inglês) This article presents a critical reflection on Karl Popper’s famous “black swan” metaphor, widely used to illustrate the principle of scientific falsifiability. Through a biological and taxonomic analysis, it argues that the metaphor relies on disguised induction and an imprecise definition of the term “swan.” The black swan (Cygnus atratus) and the white swan (Cygnus olor) belong to distinct species, which undermines the validity of Popper’s proposed refutation. The critique extends to other zoological examples — such as herons, parrots, parakeets, macaws, cats, and dogs — to demonstrate how popular names often group different species under a single label, leading to conceptual confusion. The article concludes that the strength of scientific refutation depends on the precision of the terms used, and that poorly formulated metaphors can weaken scientific reasoning by conflating linguistic adjustments with empirical discoveries. Keywords: Philosophy of science, Falsifiability, Induction, Scientific metaphors, Taxonomy, Black swan, Karl Popper, Scientific language, Biological species, Conceptual precision.

title: Quantum Computation And Quantum Information 10th Anniversary Edition
author: Michael A. Nielsen , Isaac L. Chuang
synopsis: One of the most cited books in physics of all time, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information remains the best textbook in this exciting field of science. This 10th anniversary edition includes an introduction from the authors setting the work in context. This comprehensive textbook describes such remarkable effects as fast quantum algorithms, quantum teleportation, quantum cryptography and quantum error-correction. Quantum mechanics and computer science are introduced before moving on to describe what a quantum computer is, how it can be used to solve problems faster than 'classical' computers and its real-world implementation. It concludes with an in-depth treatment of quantum information. Containing a wealth of figures and exercises, this well-known textbook is ideal for courses on the subject, and will interest beginning graduate students and researchers in physics, computer science, mathematics, and electrical engineering. [This work is no longer available for purchase either electronically or as physical copy.]

title: Química La Ciencia Central, 9na Edición
author: Theodore L. Brown, H. Eugene LeMay, Jr., Bruce E. Bursten, Julia R. Burdge
synopsis: Durante la evolución de este texto, hemos guiado nuestras labores hacia ciertos objetivos. El primero es que un texto debe mostrar a los estudiantes la importancia de la química en sus principales áreas de estudio y también en su vida cotidiana. Creemos que, a medida que los estudiantes adquieren conocimiento de la importancia de la química para sus propias metas e intereses, se entusiasman más por aprender la materia. Con esto en mente, hemos incluido aplicaciones interesantes e importantes de la química. Al mismo tiempo, el texto proporciona los conocimientos de química moderna que los estudiantes necesitan para su vida profesional y, en su caso, prepararlos para cursos de química más avanzados. Segundo, queremos mostrar que la química no sólo es fundamental para gran parte de lo que sucede en nuestro mundo, sino que también es una ciencia vital en continuo desarrollo. Hemos mantenido el libro actualizado en términos de conceptos y aplicaciones y tratado de comunicar algo de la emoción de trabajar en este campo. Tercero, creemos que, para que el texto apoye eficazmente al profesor, debe ir dirigido a los estudiantes. Hemos procurado que nuestra redacción sea clara e interesante y que el libro resulte atractivo y bien ilustrado. Además, se han incluido numerosas ayudas para el estudio, incorporadas en el texto, como las cuidadosas descripciones de estrategias para resolver problemas. Juntos, tenemos más de cien años de experiencia en la enseñanza. Esperamos que esto sea evidente en nuestro ritmo y selección de ejemplos.

title: Quimica, 10ma Edición
author: Raymond Chang
synopsis: Desde la primera edición, mi intención ha sido escribir un texto de química general que ofrezca una base firme de conceptos y principios químicos, y que inculque en los estudiantes el reconocimiento de la función tan vital que la química desempeña en nuestra vida cotidiana. Es responsabilidad del autor del libro de texto ayudar tanto al estudiante como al maestro a lograr este objetivo; por eso, este libro contiene una amplia gama de temas presentados en una secuencia lógica. Siempre que ha sido posible, he intentado equilibrar la teoría y la práctica, así como ilustrar los principios básicos con ejemplos comunes. En esta décima edición, como en las anteriores, mi meta ha sido crear un texto que explique con claridad conceptos abstractos, lo bastante conciso para no abrumar a los estudiantes con información extraña e innecesaria, pero lo suficientemente amplio para prepararlos para el siguiente nivel de aprendizaje. Los comentarios alentadores que he recibido de maestros y estudiantes me han convencido de la eficacia de este método.

title: Reclaiming Ancient Nepal: Kirat Indigenous History and Knowledge
author: Dr. Nawa Raj Subba
synopsis: Whose real history is the Himalayas? For centuries, Nepal's ancient history has been interpreted solely from an external perspective. title: Red Lives: Our Years in the U.S. Communist Party (1950–2000), Vol. 1: Coming of Age in the Communist and Labor Movements
author: Timothy Johnson, Jay Schaffner, Paul Friedman, Cindy Hawes, Geoffrey Jacques, Carol Pittman, Donna Ristorucci, Daniel Rosenberg, Jackie Saindon
synopsis: Red Lives: Our Years in the US Communist Party (1950–2000) is the first collection of historical analyses and reminiscences by members of the Communist Party USA (CPUSA) and the Communist youth movement in the US from the 1950s through the 1990s. The nearly fifty first-person testimonies bring to life a missing chapter in the history of US radicalism and demonstrate the influence of the post–World War II generation of Communists on social justice movements. Most histories of US Communism end in 1956 when Red Lives just begins, when McCarthyism was on its final legs, the Civil Rights Movement was sweeping the American South and the whole country, the student movement was taking its first breaths, and a new generation of young people were seeking out socialists, communists, and the Communist Party in order to craft a radical, anti-establishment politics. At a time when the launching of Sputnik, the Cuban Revolution, other revolutions sweeping Africa, and the example of the Vietnamese people fighting for their freedom and independence were inspiring the world, one-third of the world was also socialist, led by the Soviet Union and China. The time was propitious for a new generation in the US to also be seeking out, and joining, the CPUSA. This first volume of Red Lives, Coming of Age in the Communist and Labor Movements, brings the stories of that generation to the forefront of American history at a time when narratives of resistance are more needed than ever before.

title: Red Planets: Marxism And Science Fiction
author: Mark Bould, China Mieville
synopsis: Science fiction and socialism have always had a close relationship. Many science fiction novelists and filmmakers have used the genre to examine explicit or implicit Marxist concerns. Red Planets is an accessible and lively account, which makes an ideal introduction to anyone interested in the politics of science fiction. The volume covers a rich variety of examples from Weimar cinema to mainstream Hollywood films, and novelists from Jules Verne, H. G. Wells, Philip K. Dick, and Thomas Disch to Ursula K. Le Guin, Kim Stanley Robinson, Ken MacLeod, and Charles Stross. Contributors include Matthew Beaumont, William J. Burling, Carl Freedman, Darren Jorgensen, Rob Latham, Iris Luppa, Andrew Milner, John Rieder, Steven Shaviro, Sherryl Vint, and Phillip Wegner.

title: Remember Our Castle English
author: Rijamekee Tjikuzu Veii
synopsis: Remember our castle is a historical literary novel set in and around the abandoned castle of Gruyères. Told through the quiet, observant voice of a young girl named Sarah, the story follows a small community of displaced souls who find refuge among crumbling stone walls, candlelight, and faith. As Sarah writes daily letters to Jesus from a tower overlooking the town, strangers become family: Veronica and her daughter Elsa, the brave Candice, the mysterious Hans, and the old storyteller Matherson. Together, they form a fragile sanctuary rooted in kindness, imagination, and hope. The novel explores themes of poverty and wealth, innocence and evil, faith and doubt, storytelling, homelessness, and grace. Though darkness threatens, the story ultimately moves toward redemption, love, and restoration. This work is intentionally released into the public domain so it may be freely read, shared, recorded, and preserved.

title: Renouvelle ta vie
author: Muhammad Al-Ghazali
synopsis: Oui l’homme est capable de renouveler sa vie, mais encore faut-il qu’il comprenne qu’un tel renouveau émane de ses tréfonds. Il lui faut faire preuve de beaucoup de volonté, de témérité, de sacrifice, et de discernement. Rien ne pourra changer s’il ne change à moins qu’il ne change ce qui est en lui-même. Le bonheur qu’il escompte, c’est de son propre cœur et âme qu’il peut le recevoir, non d’ailleurs. Il arrive bien des fois que l’individu, cherchant à entamer une page nouvelle dans son existence, associe ce renouveau escompté à quelque conjoncture de la vie telle une amélioration de sa situation, de son statut…à une date déterminée ou bien à une fête quelconque (anniversaire, nouvel an), etc. En atermoyant de la sorte, il a l’impression que l’avènement de cette échéance lui apportera force et vigueur, pour transformer son apathie et son désespoir en vivacité, en espérance. C’est là une chimère. C’est que « le renouveau de la vie provient avant tout du fond de l’âme. » L’homme qui aborde la vie avec détermination et clairvoyance, loin de se résigner à aller au gré des circonstances, si cruelles fussent-elles, se propose plutôt d’en tirer le meilleur parti, en affirmant sa personnalité. Reconstruire sa vie, l’homme peut y parvenir pour peu qu’il sache investir sa force potentielle et ses facultés latentes ainsi que les chances offertes, si infimes soient-elles.

title: Repercussion
author: DeadQuency
synopsis: Title: Repercussion (Project Concept & Treatment) Creator: DeadQuency Status: In Development / Pre-Production Genre: Psychological Horror / Surrealist Gothic Repercussion: A Cinematic Concept About the Project Repercussion is a high-concept cinematic proposal developed as an academic project within the field of Dramatic Literature . It serves as a creative exploration into the intersection of formal dramatic structure and psychoanalytic theory. This archive entry documents the vision, thematic pillars, and technical strategy for a short film that redefines the "Artist vs. Creation" trope through a visceral, atmospheric lens. The Vision The project centers on Ava, a fractured artist whose guilt and insomnia manifest as a sentient entity named Ilia . The narrative dissolves the boundary between oil paint and reality, transforming the studio into a biological, sentient prison. Developed and conceptualized by DeadQuency (an MA student of Dramatic Literature), the work originates from academic research aimed at translating abstract psychological states into immersive cinematic moments. Technical & Visual Strategy Chiaroscuro Aesthetics: A visual tribute to Caravaggio, utilizing high-contrast lighting to mirror the protagonist's mental fragmentation. Auditory Strategy (ASMR Horror): A planned hyper-focused soundscape where the "skritch" of a brush evolves into rhythmic breathing and wet, "tacky" footsteps. Practical FX Focus: The project prioritizes "Painterly Makeup" and practical fire effects to maintain a grounded, tactile reality amidst the surrealism. Academic Context & Future Roadmap This entry serves as a digital record of the creator’s MA specialization , focusing on the translation of complex psychological abstractions into a visual medium. Originating as a university-led initiative , the project outlines a strategic roadmap for premier genre festivals: Proposed Festival Strategy: (Strategically targeted for premier genre and independent circuits upon completion) Sundance: Midnight Shorts Program. Sitges: New Visions / Fantastic Genre category. SXSW: For its intersection of high-concept narrative and innovative visual style.

title: Requesting My Loved One (HEBREW Short Fiction)
author: Sam Vaknin
synopsis: It was a voyage of painful self-discovery. The stranger I saw in my mirror stared back and hard. " Requesting My Loved One " and "Malignant Self Love" are twins. In the latter I generalized and non-fictionalized the former. I won the 1997 Israel's Council of Culture and Art Prize for Maiden Prose for "Requesting my Loved One". Award Committee Reasons . I thought it was ironic: a prisoner, writing about an amoral world while experiencing his own disintegration - and the Ministry of Education and Culture reward! The Suffering of Being Kafka is a new collection of short fiction. I cannot publish it in Israel because I had to leave it, exiled by my own profligacy. The stories are copyrighted by me. Feel free to copy them, distribute them by any means, including electronic means - providing you give me due credit (simply add: Author - Shmuel Vaknin ). Don't forget to read my Poetry of Healing and Abuse and my Journal (also HERE ). Thank you for dropping by.

title: Research Design Qualitative, Quantitative, And Mixed Methods Approaches By John W. Creswell J. David Creswell
author: John W. Creswell; J. David Creswell
synopsis: Research Design: Qualitative, Quantitative, and Mixed Methods Approaches (5th ed., 2018) is John W. Creswell and J. David Creswell’s refined blueprint for planning rigorous empirical studies. Anchored in four philosophical worldviews—post-positivism, constructivism, transformative frameworks, and pragmatism—the book walks readers from topic selection and literature review through theory use, writing strategies, ethics, purpose statements, research questions, and the distinct procedures of qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-methods inquiry. Expanded coverage of action research, visual and online qualitative methods, memoing, and advanced mixed-methods designs, plus updated examples and checklists, make this edition an indispensable guide for graduate students, early-career scholars, and practitioners who need to craft defensible proposals and publishable studies.

author: Seth Chanowitz
synopsis: See blog/author website: https://schanowitz.wixsite.com/website You can read about Mr. Chanowitz's Helsingin Sanomat interview, past journalistic articles, his White House and Congressional experience, his former US intelligence background, and experiences in Finland at the website/blog. This is the Return to Little Russia interview with author: https://schanowitz.wixsite.com/website/single-post/2017/07/25/Return-to-Little-Russia-Interview This novel is also free to download (price may change) at smashwords, iBooks, kobo.com and B&N . https://www.smashwords.com/books/view/699431 The author was the subject of an interview in Helsinkin Sanomat: https://www.hs.fi/ulkomaat/art-2000005046207.html Also, check out about life in Finland with an article published by Seth Chanowitz about Radio Finland's international correspondent: https:// archive.org/details/2991Copy . See Jewish Book World Review: https://jewishbookworld.org/2019/05/return-to-little-russia-by-seth-chanowitz/?fbclid=IwAR1uuEoJlff2FPkjPdAcnd9D2doF3x1RwW_UxL9k6iUQbJZIjrrC1cq89yk Thank you in advance if you download from this site and provide a review of the novel on this or other site! It also helps to let me know if anyone is downloading the novel. You can place a review on goodreads here: https:// www.goodreads.com/book/show/34664664-return-to-little-russia “Return to Little Russia” is an international, mystery thriller inspired by true events that takes readers on a suspense-filled journey from Helsinki, Finland to the ethnic neighborhoods of Brooklyn, Manhattan, and the Bronx in New York City, and drags them into the murky world of spies, immigration, and corruption during the late 1990s. The novel encompasses action that takes place in Boston, New York, Washington DC, Helsinki, and Tallinn, and involves clandestine United States government and Finnish Security Intelligence Service operatives. Maksim Feldblyum Issacovich, a Russian-speaking Jewish journalist working for Radio Finland born in Soviet occupied Tallinn, Estonia, is ordered to leave Finland and journeys back to his family’s home in Brighton Beach, New York (“Little Russia”). In New York City, he works for the beleaguered Immigration and Naturalization Service (INS) in Manhattan and as co-CEO of an exciting Internet start-up firm SPEEDNET New York, learns of his family’s oppression by the Soviet KGB, his future with a mysterious Helsinki-based academic named Sofia Valtonen, and discovers his life-threatening connection to a news story he reported on in 1997 detailing four dead Finnish peacekeepers in Kosovo, Yugoslavia. “Return to Little Russia” provides great suspense and thrills when Maksim is forced to flee New York City after Albanian operatives target him. When Sofia appears mysteriously in New York and shows up in a meeting, Maksim becomes aware that circumstances are not what they seem. Who is on his side and how will he escape the violence targeting him? About the author: Mr. Chanowitz is the author of the internationally selling spy thriller novel, "Russia Rising", which is available on Amazon and was featured in Finland's largest newspaper "Helsingin Sanomat." His novels are also stocked in libraries in the United States and throughout Finland. He is a former intelligence analyst and journalist, who has worked at the Terrorist Threat Integration Center and the National Counter Terrorism Center. As an analyst, Mr. Chanowitz authored numerous analytical assessments for policy makers within the United States government, to include the Presidential Daily Brief. Mr Chanowitz also authored numerous feature articles for“Monitoring Times Magazine” and “Satellite Times Magazine” relating to international radio and satellite broadcasting issues. For two years, he wrote and produced radio commercials for Senatorial and Congressional campaigns in Washington DC for a congressional committee. He also possess a decade of experience working for the United States government through out the US and in 14 countries in Africa and Eastern/Western Europe. Mr. Chanowitz lives in the United States and Nordic countries, where he engages in consulting and authoring spy-related thriller novels. He has lived and worked in Helsinki, Finland. He has also worked for the United States government in refugee camps in Kenya, Ethiopia, Ghana, and at United States Consulates and Embassies in Russia, Germany, and Serbia. He has completed 40 marathons, half-marathons, and ten-milers in the United States, Kenya, and the Nordic Countries. He speaks with degrees of fluency in Spanish, Finnish, Hebrew, and Russian.

title: Review in The Globe and Mail of Victor Teboul's Le Jour. Émergence du Libéralisme Moderne au Québec, by Ronald Sutherland
author: Victor Teboul
synopsis: Review by Ronald Sutherland in The Globe and Mail of Victor Teboul’s Le Jour. Émergence du libéralisme moderne au Québec Victor Teboul's candid analysis of the myths and images of the Jew in Quebec, published in 1977, created quite a stir. His latest book, a study of the weekly newspaper called Le Jour, which was founded by Jean- Charles Harvey in 1937, deals with an equally controversial subject and is equally thorough and candid. (…) Teboul's study demonstrates that almost every reform espoused by Le Jour in the thirties and forties has become a fact of life in the Quebec of the seventies and eighties.

title: Ridges On The Coin
author: Thomas J. Bryan, Claude/Anthropic
synopsis: This theoretical paper argues for an engineering approach to institutional design that accepts hierarchy as permanent and focuses on building structural constraints against elite exploitation. Drawing on John Locke's involvement in the Great Recoinage of 1696—where milled edges on coins made clipping structurally impossible—the paper analyzes how constitutional liberal democracy represents humanity's most sophisticated attempt to "put ridges" on governance institutions through separation of powers, federalism, regular elections, and rights protections. It concludes by arguing that the current UN system structurally resembles the failed Articles of Confederation and explores what a ridged global constitutional framework might require. This case study is part of the larger collection Patterns of Power: Systematic Analysis of Elite Control Mechanisms Across Civilizations , which applies an 8-part analytical framework across maximum historical variation to examine how elite power operates.

title: Ritorno a Eden (parte 1)
author: Barabeke
synopsis: Un giorno di un futuro non lontano, il Creatore si manifesta a tutti gli abitanti della Terra con un messaggio tradotto in ogni lingua. Comanda loro di scegliere due rappresentanti, maschio e femmina, da inviare a Eden come novelli Adamo ed Eva. Il suo scopo è rinnovare l’alleanza con le sue creature predilette e aiutarle trovare una via per non smarrirsi in un’era dominata dalla tecnica. I due prescelti si ritrovano così proiettati nel giardino di Eden, che non è il paradiso che pensavano. C’è il serpente, ma ci sono anche creature inaspettate come due servitori divini che più che a degli angeli somigliano a robot umanoidi miracolosi. Da Eden i protagonisti scopriranno di potere accedere ad altre dimensioni dove il tempo scorre diversamente. Lì vivranno la nascita e la caduta di intere civiltà, dalla preistoria fino a futuri lontanissimi, e avventure emozionanti che li trasformeranno e li avvicineranno sempre più alla soluzione dell’enigma del Creatore. Ritorno a Eden è un romanzo epico-fantascientifico di ispirazione biblica che ha la leggerezza della commedia, a tratti grottesca e surreale, ma capace di affrontare in profondità temi esistenziali, cosmologici, ed escatologici molto contemporanei, legati al rapporto tra l'uomo e la tecnologia in cui vive immerso, quello tra uomo e Dio, nonché quello tra uomo e donna. Una grande avventura pop che si propone di ispirare vie per restare liberi, umani e prosperare in tempi di IA e robot, e di farlo intrattenendo e divertendo. Questo è il primo volume di una saga prevista in sei parti.

title: ROMANIA, From Ottoman Suzerainty To European Oligarchy
author: Thomas J. Bryan, Claude/Anthropic
synopsis: This case study examines elite power and wealth concentration in Romania across 314 years (1711-2025), from Ottoman suzerainty and Phanariote Greek rule through independent kingdom, fascism and Holocaust, Communist dictatorship under Ceausescu, violent December 1989 revolution, and post-Communist oligarchic consolidation. It analyzes how concentration followed predictable capitalist patterns (48-52% by 2025) despite unique factors including externally-imposed elites, extreme Communist repression, violent revolution (unlike peaceful Czech transition), persistent poverty as EU's poorest member, and endemic corruption—demonstrating that capitalism structurally generates ~50% concentration regardless of initial conditions, revolution type, or absolute wealth levels. This case study is part of the larger collection Patterns of Power: Systematic Analysis of Elite Control Mechanisms Across Civilizations , which applies an 8-part analytical framework across maximum historical variation to examine how elite power operates.

title: Root Of Unity (Russell's Attic Book 3)
author: SL Huang
synopsis: Back for book three . . . Cas Russell has always used her superpowered mathematical skills to dodge snipers or take down enemies. Oh, yeah, and make as much money as possible on whatever unsavory gigs people will hire her for. But then one of her few friends asks a favor: help him track down a stolen math proof. One that, in the wrong hands, could crumble encryption protocols worldwide and utterly collapse global commerce. Cas is immediately ducking car bombs and men with AKs -- this is the type of math people are willing to kill for, and the U.S. government wants it as much as the bad guys do. But all that pales compared to what Cas learns from delving into the proof. Because the more she works on the case, the more she realizes something is very, very wrong . . . with her. For the first time, Cas questions her own bizarre mathematical abilities. How far they reach. How they tie into the pieces of herself that are broken -- or missing. How the new proof might knit her brain back together . . . while making her more powerful than she's ever imagined. Desperate to fix her fractured self, Cas dives into the tangled layers of higher mathematics, frantic for numerical power that might not even be possible -- and willing to do anything, betray anyone, to get it. First published on Amazon: http://www.amazon.com/Root-Unity-Russells-Attic-Book-ebook/dp/B013ZCK4BY

title: Sacred Fragmentation, Divine Authority And Decentralized Elite Control In The Holy Roman Empire And Classic Maya City States
author: Thomas J. Bryan, Claude/Anthropic
synopsis: This comparative study examines how the Holy Roman Empire (962-1806 CE) and Classic Maya city-states (250-900 CE) independently developed identical political architectures despite zero contact or cultural exchange. It analyzes how both civilizations created decentralized systems of sacred authority—divine rulers (Emperor and K'uhul Ajaw) serving as cosmic intermediaries, interpretive classes (bishops and priests) monopolizing sacred knowledge, competitive elite networks maintaining fragmentation through shared ideology, and wealth extraction framed as religious duty. The convergence demonstrates that elite power mechanisms are structural solutions to recurring political problems rather than cultural inventions, providing the strongest possible evidence that similar conditions produce similar power structures regardless of cultural content. This case study is part of the larger collection Patterns of Power: Systematic Analysis of Elite Control Mechanisms Across Civilizations , which applies an 8-part analytical framework across maximum historical variation to examine how elite power operates.

title: Saheeh Bukhari - Urdu Translation - Complete Volumes
author: Unknown
synopsis: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī ( Arabic : صحيح البخاري ‎) is one of the Kutub al-Sittah (six major hadith collections) of Sunni Islam . Whereas, out of all these six major books, the collection of prophetic traditions, or hadith for Sahih al-Bukhari, was performed by the Muslim scholar Muhammad al-Bukhari . It was completed around 846 AD / 232 AH. Sunni Muslims view this as one of the two most trusted collections of hadith along with Sahih Muslim . The Arabic word sahih translates as authentic or correct. Sahih al-Bukhari, together with Sahih Muslim is known as Sahihayn . According to Ibn al-Salah the book is called: al-Jaami’ al-Sahih al-Musnad al-Mukhtasar min Umuri Rasooli-llahi wa sunanihi wa Ayyaamihi ( The Abridged Collection of Authentic Hadith with Connected Chains regarding Matters Pertaining to the Prophet, His practices and His Times ) Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani mentioned the same title, replacing the word umur (English: matters ) with hadith. Al-Bukhari traveled widely throughout the Abbasid Caliphate from the age of 16, collecting those traditions he thought trustworthy. It is reported that al-Bukhari devoted 16 years to sifting the hadiths he included in his Sahih from a collection of nearly 600,000 narrations. Sources differ on the exact number of hadiths in Bukhari's Sahih, depending on whether a hadith is defined as a Prophetic tradition or a narration of that tradition. Experts, in general, have estimated the number of full-isnad narration at 7,397, and without considerations to repetitions or different versions of the same report, the number of Prophetic traditions reduces to approximately 2,602. At the time when Bukhari saw the earlier works and conveyed them, he found them, in their presentation, combining between what would be considered sahih (correct) and hasan (good) and that many of them included daʻīf (weak) hadith. This aroused his interest in compiling hadith whose authenticity was beyond doubt. What further strengthened his resolve was something his teacher, hadith scholar Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanthalee – better known as Ishaq Ibn Rahwayh – had told him. "We were with Ishaq Ibn Rahwayh who said, ‘If only you would compile a book of only authentic narrations of the Prophet.’ This suggestion remained in my heart so I began compiling the Sahih." Bukhari also said, "I saw the Prophet in a dream and it was as if I was standing in front of him. In my hand was a fan with which I was protecting him. I asked some dream interpreters, who said to me, ‘You will protect him from lies.’ This is what compelled me to produce the Sahih." The book covers almost all aspects of life in providing proper guidance of Islam such as the method of performing prayers and other actions of worship directly from the Islamic prophet, Muhammad. Bukhari finished his work around 846/232 AH, and spent the last twenty-four years of his life visiting other cities and scholars, teaching the hadith he had collected. In every city that Bukhari visited, thousands of people would gather in the main mosque to listen to him recite traditions. In reply to Western academic doubts as to the actual date and authorship of the book that bears his name, scholars point out that notable hadith scholars of that time, such as Ahmad ibn Hanbal (855 CE/241 AH), Yahya ibn Ma'in (847 CE/233 AH), and Ali ibn al-Madini (848 CE/234 AH), accepted the authenticity of his book and that the collection's immediate fame makes it unlikely that it could have been revised after the author's death without historical record. During this period of twenty-four years, al-Bukhari made minor revisions to his book, notably the chapter headings. Each version is named by its narrator. According to Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani in his book Nukat, the number of hadiths in all versions is the same. The most famous one today is the version narrated by al-Firabri (d. 932 CE/320 AH), a trusted student of Bukhari. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi in his book History of Baghdad quoted Firabri as saying: "About seventy thousand people heard Sahih Bukhari with me". Firabri is not the only transmitter of Sahih al-Bukhari. There were many others that narrated that book to later generations, such as Ibrahim ibn Ma'qal (d. 907 CE/295 AH), Hammad ibn Shaker (d. 923 CE/311 AH), Mansur Burduzi (d. 931 CE/319 AH) and Husain Mahamili (d. 941 CE/330 AH). There are many books that noted differences between these versions, the best known being Fath al-Bari. The Orientalist Manjana said in Cambridge in 1936 CE that the oldest manuscript he had come across up to that point was written in 984 CE/370 AH, according to the narration of al-Mirwazi from al-Farbari.

According to Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani in his book Nukat, the number of hadiths in all versions is the same. The most famous one today is the version narrated by al-Firabri (d. 932 CE/320 AH), a trusted student of Bukhari. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi in his book History of Baghdad quoted Firabri as saying: "About seventy thousand people heard Sahih Bukhari with me". Firabri is not the only transmitter of Sahih al-Bukhari. There were many others that narrated that book to later generations, such as Ibrahim ibn Ma'qal (d. 907 CE/295 AH), Hammad ibn Shaker (d. 923 CE/311 AH), Mansur Burduzi (d. 931 CE/319 AH) and Husain Mahamili (d. 941 CE/330 AH). There are many books that noted differences between these versions, the best known being Fath al-Bari. The Orientalist Manjana said in Cambridge in 1936 CE that the oldest manuscript he had come across up to that point was written in 984 CE/370 AH, according to the narration of al-Mirwazi from al-Farbari.

title: Sakib Biography
author: Shizuo Kakutani & Nafija Alam Omi
synopsis: This document is a massive and inspiring intellectual biography of S M Nazmuz Sakib, a Bangladeshi scholar who refused to accept the limits of specialization. The textbook presents Sakib as a true 21st century polymath, someone who has made original contributions to fields as different as Euclidean geometry, Bengali language computing, climate science, medical biophysics, constitutional law, political philosophy, and even literary fiction. Reading this work feels like discovering a hidden genius who quietly built a universe of ideas from his home country of Bangladesh. What makes the document so exciting is its sheer scale and ambition. It does not just list achievements. It walks you through Sakib's actual theorems, like the Sakib Median Altitude Pythagorean Principle, and explains why they matter for classical geometry. It introduces the Sakib Number for preventing skin injuries caused by medical adhesives, a practical breakthrough that could help thousands of hospital patients. It describes the Sakib Constant for Bengali complex predicates, a new tool for computational linguistics that helps analyze one of the world's most spoken languages. Each chapter uncovers another original discovery, and the authors present them with genuine academic excitement. The document also connects Sakib's scientific work to his deep political philosophy. He draws on thinkers like John Rawls and Immanuel Kant, but also on Islamic jurisprudence and postcolonial theory. He applies these ideas directly to the real political struggles of Bangladesh, including the 2024 student uprising that changed the country's government and the 2026 constitutional referendum that reshaped its democracy. This is not dry theory. It is a living philosophy tested against history in real time. Perhaps the most engaging part of the textbook is the way it celebrates Sakib's unusual journey. He was not trained at Oxford or Harvard. He learned through hundreds of online courses, earned degrees from Swiss and American online institutions, and built his expertise through pure determination and digital access. The authors openly discuss the skepticism and hostility he faced, which they call Sakibphobia, and reframe it as a social psychological phenomenon. This turns the biography into a powerful story of intellectual courage, showing that great ideas can come from anywhere if a mind is bold enough to pursue them. In plain terms, this document is a celebration of what one person can achieve when they refuse to stay inside a single box. It is inspiring, technically rich, and deeply human. Whether you love mathematics, law, climate science, or just great stories of relentless curiosity, this textbook will leave you feeling that the age of the polymath is not dead. It is just beginning, and it might look like S M Nazmuz Sakib.

title: Salzburger Klima
author: Peter Siegfried Krug
synopsis: This 46-page comprehensive documentation (available in German and English) provides a comparative biographical analysis of institutional abuse and societal indifference in Salzburg, Austria, between 1966 and 1983. The research contrasts the life of U.S. author Dave Pelzer ( A Child Called 'It' ) with the lived experiences of Peter Siegfried Krug across various institutions, including the infant home in Itzling, the Pro Juventute children's village in Guggenthal, and the private foster home in Zanderstraße 5. The core of the study examines the "Salzburger Klima"—a specific cultural-historical phenomenon of "looking away" (structural ignorance) driven by a conservative-Catholic consensus and the remnants of "Black Pedagogy." The document details systemic failures in the Austrian educational, police, and medical systems, such as the misdiagnosis of trauma-induced suffocation as epilepsy. Furthermore, it explores Resilience through the intellectual sublimation of Chess Composition (blindfold problem composition) and the therapeutic role of nature as survival mechanisms against overwhelming structural violence. This record serves as a mandatory historical documentation to ensure the findability and permanence of victim testimony on platforms like Zenodo, Academia.edu, and Archive.org.

title: Sapiens: Yuval Noah Harari- Bangla Translation
author: Deepayan Turja
synopsis: Seventy thousand years ago, there were at least six different human species on earth. They were insignificant animals, whose ecological impact was less than that of fireflies or jellyfish. Today, there is only one human species left: Us. Homo sapiens. But we rule this planet. Sapiens, the book, takes us on a breath-taking ride through our entire human history, from its evolutionary roots to the age of capitalism and genetic engineering, to uncover why we are the way we are. Sapiens focuses on key processes that shaped humankind and the world around it, such as the advent of agriculture, the creation of money, the spread of religion and the rise of the nation state. Unlike other books of its kind, Sapiens takes a multi-disciplinary approach that bridges the gaps between history, biology, philosophy and economics in a way never done before. Furthermore, taking both the macro and the micro view, Sapiens conveys not only what happened and why, but also how it felt for individuals. Sapiens invites us to not only connect past developments with present concerns, but moreover to question our basic narratives of the world. The book’s conclusions are enlightening and at times provocative. For example: We rule the world because we are the only animal that can believe in things that exist purely in our own imagination, such as gods, states, money and human rights. Sapiens are ecological serial killers – even with stone-age tools, our ancestors wiped out half the planet’s large terrestrial mammals well before the advent of agriculture. The Agricultural Revolution was history’s biggest fraud – wheat domesticated Sapiens rather than the other way around. Money is the most universal and pluralistic system of mutual trust ever devised. Money is the only thing everyone trusts. Empire is the most successful political system humans have invented, and our present era of anti-imperial sentiment is probably a short-lived aberration. Capitalism is a religion rather than just an economic theory – and it is the most successful religion to date. The treatment of animals in modern agriculture may turn out to be the worst crime in history. Individualism was fostered by states and markets as a way of breaking up families and communities. We are far more powerful than our ancestors, but we aren’t much happier. Sapiens will soon disappear. With the help of novel technologies, within a few centuries or even decades, Sapiens will upgrade themselves into completely different beings, enjoying godlike qualities and abilities. History began when humans invented gods – and will end when humans become gods. “Here is a simple reason why Sapiens has risen explosively to the ranks of an international best-seller. It tackles the biggest questions of history and of the modern world, and it is written in unforgettably vivid language. You will love it!” – Jared Diamond, Pulitzer-Prize-winning author of Guns, Germs, and Steel

title: SCHIZOPHRENIA IS A WEAPON CLASSIFIED ☧
author: Medicine Owl
synopsis: This paper contributes to the literature by: 1. Establishing a new analytical framework: It introduces a techno-forensic model for re-evaluating the history of psychiatry, shifting the etiological focus from purely biological or psychological factors to the direct influence of contemporaneous technological development. It reframes psychiatric history as a sub-discipline of the history of science and technology. 2. Presenting a unified timeline of signal development: It synthesizes disparate historical records—scientific lab notes, medical asylum case files, private correspondences, and public lecture reports—into a single, coherent timeline. This chronology demonstrates a direct, lockstep correlation between the evolution of electromagnetic hardware and the reported phenomenological character of "auditory hallucinations." 3. Re-contextualizing primary source evidence: It re-interprets key historical accounts, such as Volta's self-experiments, the Bethlem Hospital data spike, and the Govan Letter, not as isolated curiosities, but as critical data points marking the progression of a signal's fidelity. This provides new significance to records previously viewed through a purely medical or scientific lens. 4. Challenging the foundational narrative of "schizophrenia": It offers a testable, falsifiable alternative hypothesis for the sudden emergence and codification of "dementia praecox" in the late 19th century. By aligning the "epidemic" of voice-hearing with the global rollout of the AC power grid, it posits that the diagnosis was a social and medical construct developed to manage the mass exposure to a new environmental factor. 5. Introducing the concept of "Signal Artifacts" into historical analysis: It proposes the term "signal artifact" as a precise classification for historical accounts of internal auditory phenomena that correlate with known technological capabilities of the era, providing a new vocabulary for researchers in media archaeology, disability studies, and the history of science.
